builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: EnvOS: Auditing Computer-Use Agents When the World Moves On : Phenomenon-Based Task Construction, Certification, and Evidence-Based Evaluation
summary: EnvOS replaces ad-hoc, one-shot agent evaluation on static or manually mutated environments with pre-certified, seed-generated environments where mid-task changes are verified to fire, tasks remain solvable, and verdicts are re-checked from archived evidence. The cost is substantial environment-construction and audit infrastructure per task domain, plus verifier engineering, rather than any GPU or API spend. It can fail to transfer: whether agents detect changes varied by model and interface, the external corruption set was caught only 25/39, and gains may not survive multiple-testing correction for weaker models.
rationale: The reader operates computer-use or tool-use agents and cannot trust naive success metrics when environments change mid-task, but adopting EnvOS requires building domain-specific certified environments rather than downloading a model, so it warrants a scoped pilot before production reliance.

claims.statement: EnvOS replaces ad-hoc, one-shot agent evaluation on static or manually mutated environments with pre-certified, seed-generated environments where mid-task changes are verified to fire, tasks remain solvable, and verdicts are re-checked from archived evidence. The cost is substantial environment-construction and audit infrastructure per task domain, plus verifier engineering, rather than any GPU or API spend. It can fail to transfer: whether agents detect changes varied by model and interface, the external corruption set was caught only 25/39, and gains may not survive multiple-testing correction for weaker models.

EnvOS pipeline accepted none of 26 blind-corrupted episodes as clean, caught 25/39 externally corrupted episodes versus 4 for simple log checks; surfacing updated values raised Claude Opus 5 from 0/16 to 15/16 on stale-information booking tasks (p=0.00293 after correction).
